Clauses on x and t, for all 32 types: symmetries found by brute force on the Cartan matrix. t is accepted exactly for the symmetries of order at most 2. This set equals the one T13's picker offers (involutions mapped to labels) on every type. Order-3 symmetries are refused (D4 t=3.2.4.1). Also refused: non-symmetries (cyclic shift, A3 t=2.1.3, B3 t=3.2.1, C2 and G2 t=2.1, E6 t=6.2.3.4.5.1), lists one short and one long, positions instead of labels (A3 t=2.1.0), and an empty t. Accepted: the D4 swaps, E6 t=6.2.5.4.3.1 and A3 t=3.2.1.

x: an empty x is accepted. x=0 and x=n+1 are refused on every type, as are -1, a, 1.5, 1..2, .1, 1., 1,2, 1e0, 0x1, %201, 1%20, +1, Infinity and D4 x=2.9. Boards T13 does not offer are refused: A2~, B3~, C2~, D4^(3), pentagon, square, c: matrices, A9, A12, D9, E9, a3, A03, E5, D3, B1, C1.

notes: Environment, affects every agent: Astro 7 builds use Node's compile cache in the shared /tmp/node-compile-cache, whose directory was so large that a listing took more than 2 minutes. Every agent's astro build sat in rename() in disk sleep for more than 10 minutes. Building with NODE_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE=1 took 66 s. The orchestrator may want to set this, or a per-agent NODE_COMPILE_CACHE, for all lenses.

History, known family: exampleLoaded cancels a pending burst (a decision recorded by P1-A2; site/tests/unit/history.test.ts asserts 'A pending burst is not written after the push'). So a move followed within 500 ms by an example or catalogue load never reaches any history entry, and Back from the example returns to the state before the move. This is the same family as the owner's open item in DECISIONS.md (MERGE, phase 5 round: 'A move followed by Back within the 500 ms burst ... loses the move').

T14 registry: the 'default' preset has a caption and no state field (CONTRACTS 6: 'T1 and T14 have no presets', but collectRegistry requires a default). It is not a ToolState: encodeState of it throws, and round 1's attack-39 unit test fails on 'atlas preset default'. Nothing on the site encodes it.

AtlasPicker Cite cites location.href, a choice recorded in decisions/P6-A4.md. So /tools/atlas/?g=E9 is cited with ?g=E9 (a link that shows the notice), and foreign parameters and the fragment are kept (?g=B3&utm_source=x#top). The tool routes' Cite uses linkFor, which drops the instance's unreadable keys.

Embed 'Open on the site' sets its href to /tools/<id>/ plus location.search (the plan says 'with the same query'). Within the 500 ms burst after a move it opens the state before the move. Copy link has no such window.

Keys of other tools (lens section 6; the spec does not settle them): T13 validates keys it then drops. s without c, w=4, k=4, v=p&m=l and c=p&s=1,0,0&m=r&w=1 give the notice on /tools/satake. c=n&s=1,1,1&w=1.2, k=3, y=3.2.1, r=1.0.0 and j=coxeter are dropped silently. The picker validates such keys against its placeholder board A1, so /tools/atlas/?x=2 shows the notice. T11 ignores a parseable m and T12 drops v and m (both recorded plan rules), so g=A2&v=p&m=l loads with no notice on /tools/fold and /tools/rep but shows the notice elsewhere.

Copy link from one lesson instance keeps another instance's unreadable keys as the bar holds them (design of history.ts). On M9, after ?b10.x=1&b1.g=E9, b10's Copy link still carries b1.g=E9, so the copied link shows b1's notice again.
